title: In 711 a king vanished in battle. Spain changed for eight centuries.

beats.text: In 711 a king vanished in battle. Spain changed for eight centuries.
Around the year 700, Spain belonged to the Visigoths: Germanic kings with jewelled crowns, ruling from Toledo. Their nobles were at each other's throats.
Legend blames a woman. Count Julian's daughter, wronged by King Roderic. To take revenge, Julian opened the door to Africa.
In 711, a Berber commander, Tariq ibn Ziyad, crossed the strait with a small army. The rock where he landed still carries his name: Jabal Tariq. Gibraltar.
King Roderic rushed south. At the river Guadalete, his army was routed. The king died, and his body was never found.
Within a few years, almost the whole peninsula was under Muslim rule. It became al-Andalus.
Muslim rule in Spain would last nearly eight centuries, until 1492.
beats.say: Muslim rule in Spain would last nearly eight centuries, until fourteen ninety-two.

beats.text: Only a few mountain valleys in the far north never fell.
